top10.introHtml: Ten best buys from 82 four-seat convertibles between $7,000 and $15,000 within 35 miles of Media, PA. Ranked for a fun second car: sound model family first, then mileage, price and distance. Notes are based on listing data and known model issues; none of these cars has been inspected.

picks.whyGood: E93 3 Series with the naturally aspirated N52 six, the most durable engine BMW offered in this era, at under 90K miles. CarGurus rates it a Great Deal and it is the cheapest sound car in today's pool.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. The folding hardtop is hydraulic: listen for a straining pump and look for fluid in the trunk. Check the valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets for leaks, and confirm the electric water pump has been replaced.
picks.bottomLine: Best value on the board at $7,425 if the roof cycles cleanly and service records exist.

picks.whyGood: Only 54,896 miles on a 2009 Eos Lux, with clean-title and no-accident filters applied on Cars.com. Hardtop with a built-in sunroof makes it a real four-season car.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. The Eos roof is the whole risk: clear the roof drains, check every seal for shrinkage, and look for damp footwells. Ask about timing chain tensioner and DSG service history on the 2.0T.
picks.bottomLine: Low miles make this the Eos to consider, but only after a wet-weather leak check.

picks.whyGood: A 1995 XJS 2+2 with just 46,103 miles, from the final and best-sorted years of the model. Clean-title and no-accident filters applied; a genuine classic at used-economy-car money.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. Rust is the killer: check rear arches, sills and floor pans. Confirm which engine it has (the 4.0 six is far cheaper to keep than the V12), look for cooling system neglect, and test every electrical switch.
picks.bottomLine: The character pick of the list; buy on condition and records, not on the odometer alone.

picks.whyGood: E46 330Ci with the M54 3.0 six and only 64,358 miles, which is very low for a 2003. The E46 is one of the best-driving 4-seat convertibles in this budget and parts are cheap and plentiful.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. Check the soft-top hydraulic rams and motor, the cooling system (expansion tank, water pump, hoses are wear items), valve cover and oil filter housing leaks, and rear subframe mounts for cracks.
picks.bottomLine: A low-mile E46 at $9,495 is a strong buy if the cooling system has been refreshed.

picks.whyGood: 2012 A5 2.0T quattro Premium Plus at about 87K miles: all-wheel drive, a well-insulated soft top and a modern cabin. Clean-title and no-accident filters applied.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. The 2.0T of this era is known for oil consumption and timing chain tensioner wear, so ask for consumption test results or proof of the piston/tensioner fix. Check the top's hydraulic operation and rear-window bond.
picks.bottomLine: A handsome year-round convertible, worth it only with documented engine service.

picks.whyGood: 2010 S5 Cabriolet with the supercharged 3.0T V6 and quattro at 92K miles. Fast, refined and rare at $10,489.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. Budget for the 7-speed S tronic mechatronic unit and service history, check for thermostat and water pump leaks, PCV failure and carbon build-up. Confirm accident history, which this listing does not state.
picks.bottomLine: The most car for the money here, with running costs to match; get a specialist inspection.

picks.whyGood: Just 8 miles from Media, a late 2013 Eos at $9,797 with under 100K miles. Final-years cars got the updated front end and the most sorted version of the roof.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. Clear the roof drains and inspect all roof seals, look for damp carpets, and ask for DSG fluid service and timing chain tensioner records.
picks.bottomLine: The easiest car on the list to go see; worth a look if the roof is dry and quiet.

picks.whyGood: 2012 650i xDrive convertible at 90K miles for $11,742, with no accidents reported. A six-figure grand tourer when new, with real rear seats and all-wheel drive.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. The N63 twin-turbo V8 is the concern: check for oil consumption, valve stem seal smoke on startup, injector and battery history, and confirm BMW's customer care package work was done.
picks.bottomLine: Huge presence for the price, but only buy with full engine records and a repair reserve.

picks.whyGood: 2008 135i with only 48,371 miles: twin-turbo N54 six in the smallest BMW convertible body. Clean-title and no-accident filters applied, and it is the lowest-mile BMW in the pool.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. N54 gotchas: high-pressure fuel pump, injectors, wastegate rattle and water pump. Check the soft-top hydraulics and oil filter housing gasket.
picks.bottomLine: The enthusiast's choice; low miles justify the price if the N54 items are documented.

picks.whyGood: 2005 XK8 with 51,549 miles, from the last model year with the improved 4.2 V8 and 6-speed automatic. Clean-title and no-accident filters applied.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. Check the convertible top hydraulic lines (the notorious 'green shower' leak at the header), front suspension bushings, and for rust at the front floor and rear arches.
picks.bottomLine: A lot of elegance for $11,950; the 4.2 cars are the ones to have.

manual10.introHtml: Three confirmed manual-transmission convertibles surfaced on this refresh, all from CarGurus. A fourth, a 2011 BMW 335i 6-speed at $10,995, was left out because its listing has no photo.

picks.whyGood: 2011 135i with a manual gearbox and 75,522 miles. 2011 brought the single-turbo N55, which is easier to live with than the earlier N54, and three pedals are rare on these.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. Manual checks: clutch bite point (high means worn), slow 2nd/3rd shifts for synchro wear, throw-out bearing chirp, and weeping clutch hydraulics. Also check the oil filter housing gasket, water pump and the soft-top hydraulics.
picks.bottomLine: The best manual on the board: quick, compact and reasonably priced at $12,500.

picks.whyGood: 2010 Mustang GT with the 4.6 V8 and a 5-speed manual, 9.5 miles from Media. Simple, tough drivetrain with cheap parts everywhere.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. Manual checks: clutch bite point (high means worn), slow 2nd/3rd shifts for synchro wear, throw-out bearing chirp, and weeping clutch hydraulics. Listen for 8.8 axle clunk on takeoff and cam-phaser rattle at idle; check spring perches for rust. At 132K miles ask what has been replaced.
picks.bottomLine: V8 and a stick for $11,495 close to home; the miles are the only reservation.

picks.whyGood: 2012 128i with a 6-speed manual and 86,671 miles. The N52 six has no turbos to fail and is the most dependable engine in the 1 Series range.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. Manual checks: clutch bite point (high means worn), slow 2nd/3rd shifts for synchro wear, throw-out bearing chirp, and weeping clutch hydraulics. Check the valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets, the electric water pump, and the soft-top hydraulics.
picks.bottomLine: The sensible manual: less power than the 135i but the lowest ownership risk.

mustangs.introHtml: Ford Mustang convertibles, 2005 and newer only, $7,000 to $15,000 within 35 miles of ZIP 19063. Top five of the Mustangs found today.

picks.whyGood: Cheapest 2005+ Mustang today at $9,142. The 2011-2014 3.7 V6 makes 305 hp and is very durable; no accidents reported.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. Listen for 8.8 axle clunk on takeoff, check spring perches for rust, top-latch wear and water staining on the rear seats. At 121K miles confirm transmission fluid service and check for water pump seepage.
picks.bottomLine: The budget entry to a late S197; fine if the top and underside are clean.

picks.whyGood: 2011 Premium trim with leather and the then-new 305 hp 3.7 V6, no accidents reported, at $9,990.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. Listen for 8.8 axle clunk on takeoff, check spring perches for rust, top-latch wear and water staining on the rear seats. At 119K miles check the transmission for harsh shifts and ask for fluid service history.
picks.bottomLine: Nicer interior than the base cars for under $10K.

picks.whyGood: The only V8 manual in the group: 2010 GT with the 4.6 and a 5-speed, 9.5 miles from Media.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. Listen for 8.8 axle clunk on takeoff, check spring perches for rust, top-latch wear and water staining on the rear seats. Listen for cam-phaser rattle at idle on the 3-valve 4.6 and check the clutch bite point.
picks.bottomLine: The driver's pick of the Mustangs at $11,495, high miles noted.

picks.whyGood: 2014 was the last S197 year, with the 3.7 V6 and no accidents reported, at $10,437.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. Listen for 8.8 axle clunk on takeoff, check spring perches for rust, top-latch wear and water staining on the rear seats. Farthest from Media at 34 miles; at 128K miles confirm fluid services before making the trip.
picks.bottomLine: A fair price for a final-year car, though the $9,142 example undercuts it.

picks.whyGood: 2010 GT with just 80K miles, 10 miles from Media, no accidents reported. The lowest-mile V8 Mustang in budget.
picks.whatToVerify: Cycle the top fully up and down twice, check headliner and carpets for water stains, inspect the rear-window seam and the rockers for rust. Listen for 8.8 axle clunk on takeoff, check spring perches for rust, top-latch wear and water staining on the rear seats. Listen for cam-phaser rattle at idle on the 3-valve 4.6 and confirm the transmission type on the listing.
picks.bottomLine: The cleanest GT here; worth the $13,835 if you want V8 sound and lower miles.
